published_by: EMR Delivery Body / NESO (auction results), reported via Ofgem Annex 9 v1.8 'Historical level tables' and market analysts' auction reviews
what_this_is: THE PUBLISHED AUCTION OUTCOME, NOT A READING OF IT. The GB Capacity Market clearing price for each delivery year, held SEPARATELY for the T-4 (four-years-ahead) and T-1 (one-year-ahead) auctions, in the unit the auctions clear in: GBP per kW per year of DE-RATED capacity. Nothing here interprets them. Which auction a given unit holds an agreement in, the de-rating factor applied to its class, whether it won an agreement at all, and what an aggregator passes through to a member are all READINGS, and each lane owns its own.

basis.units: GBP per kW per YEAR, applied to DE-RATED capacity under an awarded agreement. NOT per kW of rated or nameplate power, and NOT an energy price.
basis.year_key: delivery_year is the calendar year the CM delivery year COMMENCES. The GB delivery year runs 1 October to 30 September, so delivery_year 2022 is DY 2022/23 and runs 2022-10-01 to 2023-09-30. This is NOT the year the auction was held: a T-4 for delivery_year 2023 was held in early 2020, and a T-1 for delivery_year 2023 was held in early 2023.
basis.t4_vs_t1: TWO SEPARATE AUCTIONS FOR THE SAME DELIVERY YEAR, at different prices, and they must not be averaged or conflated. T-4 procures the bulk of capacity four years ahead; T-1 tops up one year ahead against a revised requirement, is much smaller, and is far more volatile because it is bid against a known-tight margin. In DY 2022/23 the T-1 cleared 11.6x the T-3 for the same delivery year.
basis.price_cap: T-1 auctions clear against a price cap. DY 2022/23's T-1 cleared AT the cap (GBP75/kW), so that figure is a censored observation: it records where the cap sat, not where supply and demand crossed. A model that reads it as a market price has read a regulatory ceiling as a market outcome.

why_native_units: The quantity a CM participant actually earns is clearing_price x DE-RATED capacity x (agreement held), and no publication states that product for any particular unit. Carrying only the clearing price forces every consumer to perform the de-rating and the agreement condition itself, so both are under test in the lane that does them. That is exactly where the defect of 2026-09-07 lived: `company/market/flexibility_potential.py` multiplied GBP75/kW by a household's RATED asset power with no de-rating and no agreement, producing GBP930/household/year from a capped T-1 result for a delivery year the constant's own comment did not name.

provenance_legend.primary: read from the EMR Delivery Body / NESO auction result publication for THIS delivery year. THERE ARE NONE IN THIS FILE -- see `primary_not_reached` below.
provenance_legend.secondary: read from a publication that QUOTES the auction result -- an Ofgem annex's notes column, or a market analyst's auction review -- rather than from the auction result itself. Every asserted value here is secondary, and that is a stated limit of this artefact, not an oversight.
provenance_legend.contested: two secondary sources give different figures for the same auction and this pass did not reconcile them. Carried as NULL with both figures named. NEVER averaged.
provenance_legend.not_applicable: no auction of this type procured for this delivery year. Distinct from an unknown price and distinct from zero.

primary_not_reached: The EMR Delivery Body register (emrdeliverybody.com) returned HTTP 403 to this pass on 2026-09-07, so no figure here was read from the publisher's own auction result. Upgrading these entries from `secondary` to `primary` is the next pass on this artefact, and until it happens every consumer is reading an analyst's or an annex's restatement.

participation_rules.minimum_cmu_capacity_note: The minimum capacity threshold for a Capacity Market Unit was reduced from 2 MW to 1 MW, reflecting the deployment of smaller distributed resources. A unit below the threshold cannot hold an agreement in its own right and can reach the auction only by being aggregated, as a Component, into a DSR CMU that meets it.
participation_rules.minimum_cmu_capacity_source: Electricity Capacity (Amendment) Regulations 2020 explanatory note (legislation.gov.uk) and CMS 'Capacity Market: consultation on future improvements'
participation_rules.domestic_households_note: A GB domestic household cannot hold a Capacity Market agreement. Whole-house flexible load is single-digit kW against a 1,000 kW minimum CMU, so at least ~80 households are needed to reach the smallest unit that can prequalify. A household reaches the CM only inside an aggregator's DSR CMU, and NO PUBLICATION STATES WHAT AN AGGREGATOR PASSES THROUGH to a member household -- the commercial terms are bilateral. The clearing prices in this file therefore do not, on their own, support any per-household revenue figure.
participation_rules.derating: The CM pays on DE-RATED capacity, not rated capacity. De-rating factors are published per auction and per technology class, and for DSR and storage they are duration-dependent. NOT IN THIS ARTEFACT: no de-rating factor was fetched by this pass, so any consumer applying these prices to a rated power figure is overstating by the whole de-rating factor and must say so.
